verdicts.summary: Branch re-check discards a read that straddles a switch, and the discard leaves a non-marker null remote, so recovery works.
verdicts.scenario: Switch A to B during remoteStatus. currentBranch before and after differ, so refreshLocalStatusCore runs and readRemoteStatus returns null. updateCachedRemoteStatus(null) stores remote: null, and the next getStatus or refresh reloads it. Detached HEAD: symbolic-ref exits 1 and returns null on both reads, so there is no spurious mismatch. A symbolic-ref failure other than exit 0 or 1 errors the refresh, but the local snapshot is already published.

verdicts.summary: The local snapshot is now published before the lock, as intended. Whether a PR lookup holding the lock is time-bounded lives in GitManager or the provider code, and I did not trace it. That unboundedness existed before this change.
verdicts.missing: Timeout behaviour of workflow.remoteStatus (GitManager PR lookup and gh/provider calls) while it holds the per-cwd remote write lock.

verdicts.summary: The local-only path reads `previous` before taking the lock. It can then overwrite a remote that a concurrent writer cached while it waited.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The cache has no remote. 2) A poll or getStatus holds the remote write lock and is reading the remote. 3) vcsRefreshStatus {localOnly:true} reads `previous` at line 487 (remote null) and publishes local. 4) It waits for the lock. 5) The poll finishes and caches a real PR, ahead and behind. 6) The local-only call gets the lock, sees `!previous?.remote` is true from the stale snapshot, and writes the null marker with publish. 7) The UI's PR and ahead/behind are wiped, and the null marker blocks reloads (see finding 0).
verdicts.consequence: A valid PR and ahead/behind state is erased and published as null, and it may stay hidden until a full refresh. The staleness comes from reading `previous` outside the lock. Re-reading the cache inside the lock avoids it.
